recentItems.title: We Don't Handicap People. We Handicap Environments. | Isaac Jean-Paul | TEDxBeverly Grove
recentItems.description:
Paralympic medalist Isaac Jean-Paul opened his TEDxBeverlyGrove 2026 talk with the doctor who diagnosed him legally blind at two, then told his parents not to hold him back because of what they thought he could not do. What followed was not an inspiration story. It was a case against what he calls the kindness ceiling, when help quietly lowers the standard. Drawing on the coaches who raised his ceiling and the athletes he later coached, Jean-Paul closes with the line that gives the talk its title: we don't handicap people, we handicap environments. Isaac Jean-Paul is a two-time Paralympic medalist (bronze, Tokyo 2020; silver, Paris 2024), world-record holder in high jump, and World Champion (2017 World Para Athletics Championships). He is an NCAA Division II national champion, All-American, and is currently
training to become the first Paralympian to win Olympic gold at the LA 2028 Olympic Games.

At TEDxBeverlyGrove
Isaac Jean-Paul will share “We Don’t Handicap People. We Handicap Environments.” His claim is blunt: performance is shaped less by labels than by the ceilings built around them—lowered expectations, overprotection, and systems that quietly train limitation. You’ll leave with a sharper lens for what to redesign—at home, at work, and in your own standards—so potential has room to show up. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Generosity Paradox | Andrew Dayton | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if the way we give is getting in the way of the change we want to create?

Andrew Dayton challenges the idea that wealth should be treated as a proxy for wisdom in philanthropy. Instead, he argues for giving guided by evidence, measurable outcomes, and the wisdom of the communities closest to the problems.

By focusing less on donor preferences and more on what actually works, philanthropy can help prove solutions that lead to broader, lasting change.

Sometimes, the most powerful thing a donor can do is step out of the way.
 Andrew Dayton is the founder and CEO of the Constellation Fund, a Minnesota-based foundation dedicated to effective poverty alleviation. Constellation deploys rigorous data and analytics to identify, fund, and empower the people and organizations making the greatest measurable impact on poverty in the Twin Cities. Through its research arm, CoLab, Constellation also catalyzes and funds longitudinal research on what actually drives economic mobility.

Before founding Constellation, Andrew served as Deputy Legislative Director to former San Francisco Mayor Edwin M. Lee, directing the city's state and federal policy priorities in Sacramento and Washington D.C. He previously co-owned a trio of award-winning hospitality and retail businesses in the Twin Cities.

Andrew holds a B.A. in History from Yale University and a J.D. from the University of Michigan Law School. He lives in Minneapolis with his wife and daughters. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Designing Tomorrow's Harvest: AI and a New Era of Crop Engineering | Scott Jackson | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
In a world grappling with climate extremes, soil depletion, and food security demands, we can no longer rely solely on traditional breeding. Scott Jackson, founder of the Institute for Crop Design at the University of Georgia, shares how AI-powered modeling, precision genome engineering, and next-generation plant breeding are ushering in a new era of intentional crop design. Drawing from decades of experience—from sequencing legume genomes to leading R&D teams in the seed industry and now building disruptive solutions at UGA—he demonstrates real-world examples. This talk explores the design-build-test-learn cycle that accelerates innovation, turning data, biology, and breeding into tools for resilient, high-value crops. Discover how we move from selecting nature’s offerings to designing the abundant, sustainable food systems of tomorrow. Scott Jackson is a plant geneticist, agricultural innovator, and Georgia Research Alliance Eminent Scholar in Synthetic Biology at the University of Georgia. His work sits at the intersection of genetics, biotechnology, and crop improvement, exploring how advances in science can help design better plants for a changing world.

Over a career spanning academia and the seed industry, Jackson has helped advance the genetic understanding of important crops, including legumes and peanuts, and has contributed to landmark efforts to sequence crop genomes. His research focuses on turning that genetic knowledge into practical tools for improving crops and accelerating the pace of agricultural innovation.

Today, Jackson is helping build the next generation of crop design, bringing together plant genetics, biotechnology, data, and emerging technologies to move agriculture from selecting the traits nature provides to intentionally designing the traits tomorrow's crops will need. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why renewing the American Dream runs through rural America | Tony Pipa | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
As our country celebrates its 250th birthday, too many of us feel as if the American Dream is dying. Yet the American Dream is not just about financial success – it’s about creating a good society where the opportunity to achieve is held in common.

In this talk, Tony Pipa, host of the Reimagine Rural podcast and founder of the Reimagining Rural Policy initiative at the Brookings Institution, describes how rural communities are demonstrating that renewal of the American Dream relies on healthy civic structures, where people use their talents, capabilities, and creativity to keep their hometowns vibrant and vital. In an era of polarization and pessimism, he tells the story of places in rural America undergoing a civic renaissance that offer a path forward for the rest of the country – if we embrace it. Tony Pipa is a senior fellow in the Center for Sustainable Development at the Brookings Institution. Pipa launched and leads the Reimagining Rural Policy initiative and hosts the award-winning Reimagine Rural podcast. He also provides expertise on U.S. global development policy and local implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), reflected in the work of the SDG Leadership Cities Network.

The Reimagining Rural Policy initiative provides analysis and recommendations to improve the effectiveness of federal policy in supporting rural communities in the 21st century. The stories profiled by the Reimagine Rural podcast feature local people developing solutions to strengthen the resilience, economic security, and future prospects of their rural towns. As part of this portfolio to improve rural policy, Pipa is helping lead and facilitate America’s Rural Future: The Brookings-AEI Commission on Rural Prosperity, co-chaired by former Senator Heidi Heitkamp (D-ND) and former governor Chris Sununu (R-NH).

Pipa came to Brookings after serving as chief strategy officer at the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and as a special envoy at the U.S. Department of State, leading the U.S. delegation during the intergovernmental negotiations at the U.N. to agree upon the SDGs.

His work on global policy built upon decades of leadership advancing community and economic development at home. He served as the first director of philanthropic services at the Triangle Community Foundation; founding CEO of the Warner Foundation in Durham, North Carolina; and as a founder of the Foundation for Louisiana.

He serves as vice-chair of StriveTogether, chair of the Reimagining Rural Assistance Network (RRAN), treasurer at Lead for America, member of the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond’s Rural Investment Collaborative, member of the NC Textile Innovation and Sustainability Engine’s advisory council, and on other advisory councils and boards related to economic mobility. He grew up in rural Elysburg, Pennsylvania, attended Stanford University, graduated from Duke University, and earned a Master of Public Administration at the Harvard Kennedy School. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Blame the voters. | Rob Port | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
We often blame politicians, billionaires, lobbyists, the media, or social media for the problems facing our communities and our country. But what if we're overlooking the most important part of the equation: ourselves?

Political columnist and writer Rob Port takes a provocative look at modern American politics and argues that voters have more responsibility for the government they criticize than they may want to admit.

From the national debt and competing demands for taxes and government services to the influence of social media and the high rate at which incumbents are reelected, Port examines the tension between what Americans say they want from government and the choices they make at the ballot box.

His challenge is uncomfortable but straightforward: democracy doesn't just ask us to choose our leaders. It asks us to take responsibility for the choices we make. Rob Port was a pioneer in political blogging in North Dakota, founding SayAnythingBlog.com in 2003. Before beginning his writing career, he spent 10 years working as a private investigator specializing in insurance fraud, accessing public records, and criminal defense.

He publishes digital and print columns covering North Dakota government and politic in publications across the state, and also hosts the Plain Talk podcast along with his co-host Chad Oban. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Are you flying high? | Terry Brandt | TEDxFargo
recentItems.description:
What if your calling isn't one perfect destination, but something that changes as you do?

Terry Brandt begins with the remarkable story of Larry Walters, who attached weather balloons to a lawn chair to pursue his dream of flying. What started as a short trip above his neighborhood unexpectedly carried him 16,000 feet into the sky—and into a dramatic rescue. But for Terry, Walters' story is about more than a homemade flying machine. It's about being willing to pursue a dream while still being “wonderfully scared.”

Drawing from Lutheran theology and his own journey from teacher to pastor, camp director, bishop, and foundation executive, Terry offers a different way to think about calling. Rather than a single point we can either find or miss, calling exists at the intersection of our gifts, our passions, and the needs of the world—and those things are always changing.

Terry explores how listening both inwardly and to the people who know us best can help reveal where we're being called next. His challenge is simple: have the conversation, dream a little bigger, and be willing to move forward even when you're wonderfully scared. Rev. Dr. Terry A. Brandt believes that transformation happens when people create space for vision, risk holy experiments, and trust that something sacred can emerge in the process.

As the Executive Director of the Offutt Family Foundation, Terry leads with a conviction that generosity is one of the most powerful forces for good in the world. He guides the Foundation’s efforts to strengthen communities and expand opportunity, helping people and ideas flourish in ways that make a lasting difference.

Before stepping into his work with Ron Offutt and his family, Terry served as Vice President for Advancement at Concordia College in Moorhead and earlier as a bishop of the Eastern North Dakota Synod in the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America. Those experiences shaped his deep belief that leadership is ultimately about relationship, namely listening well, calling out the gifts of others, and inspiring people to imagine what’s possible together.

Terry’s path has never fit into a single category. He has been a pastor, entrepreneur, educator, and strategist, each role forming part of a lifelong commitment to bridging faith and innovation. He often describes himself as a “flipper and fixer,” not just of houses (his past time) but of systems, cultures, and stories that need new energy and vision.

Today, Terry continues to explore how purpose, generosity, and imagination can renew institutions and communities alike. He brings humor, humility, and a deep sense of hope to every conversation believing that real change begins not with certainty, but with the courage to begin.

Terry is married to Kristi Brandt, principal of Fargo South High School.  Together, they have three children, Lindsay, Kallie, Austin and a beloved English Bulldog with a face that only a mother could love named Stella. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Power of Rage | Célia Kamdom | TEDxFredrikstad
recentItems.description: We are often told to let anger go, stay calm and be the bigger person. Célia Kamdom asks a different question: what if rage can be transformed instead of swallowed? She explores the energy behind revenge and the choice to redirect it away from destruction and toward creation. The result is not a celebration of anger, but a reframing of what we can do with it. Sometimes the most powerful response to what hurt us is to build something real. A life, a project or a future that becomes its own answer. Célia Kamdom is a technology professional, entrepreneur and founder of Oriaku Studio, a design brand connecting African craftsmanship with Scandinavian minimalism. Her professional background spans technology, change management and entrepreneurship, while her creative work is rooted in questions of heritage, recognition and making something new from competing worlds. In her TEDx talk, Célia turns to another powerful source of creative energy: rage. Rather than romanticizing anger or treating it as destruction, she asks what becomes possible when the energy behind revenge is redirected toward building a life, a project or a future that did not exist before. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Decision: Breaking the Cycle of Avoidance | Raissa Pahlevi | TEDxAvicenna Cinere School
recentItems.description:
What if the small decisions you make every day are quietly shaping the person you become? 

This emotional and personal talk explores how fear of judgment can turn into a cycle of avoidance and what happens when we finally choose to move forward, even while we are still afraid.

In this personal and thought provoking talk, Raissa Pahlevi reflects on a moment when she wanted to step onto the stage but chose to stay backstage, revealing how fear of judgment can shape not only our decisions, but also the way we see ourselves.

Blending her personal experience with insights from psychology, Raissa explores the spotlight effect, the brain’s response to fear, and the reinforcement loop that can make avoidance feel like a natural choice. 

She invites us to look closer at the small decisions we make every day and asks whether we are truly choosing what we want or simply choosing what feels safe

 Raissa Pahlevi is a 15 year old student at Avicenna Cinere Junior High School. She loves exploring new experiences and connecting with others through her friendly and approachable personality. However, many of her thoughts and aspirations have often been quietly held back by hesitation and self-doubt.

Through academics, sports, and everyday challenges, she has come to understand that fear is not always something to overcome, but something to grow alongside. This perspective inspired her TEDx Talks, in which she explores how fear, often seen as something negative, can quietly shape our growth and lead us toward unexpected opportunities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How not to travel | Gunnar Garfors | TEDxFredrikstad
recentItems.description: After travelling to every country in the world twice, Gunnar Garfors has learned a surprising amount about how not to travel. He shares the mistakes, misunderstandings and small scandals that taught him why copying the same social-media itineraries can flatten the very thing we travel to experience. With humor and hard-earned perspective, he argues for more independent travel: talk to people, leave space for surprise, and stop outsourcing your holiday to someone else's feed. Meaningful travel often begins when we stop following the herd. Gunnar Garfors is a Norwegian author, world-record traveller and founder of The Garfors Globe. He has travelled to every country in the world twice and spent years on the road collecting both extraordinary experiences and spectacular mistakes. His books and talks focus less on ticking places off a list than on how we meet people and cultures once we arrive. Having repeatedly misunderstood customs, taken the wrong route and learned the hard way, Gunnar makes a humorous case against copycat tourism and for journeys shaped by curiosity rather than someone else's highlight reel. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: A common Destiny  | Chapi Mwango | TEDxArada Play
recentItems.description:
What if the story of your life didn’t begin with you?

A Common Destiny explores the connections between our personal stories and the stories that came before us. Through CHAPI MWANGO, the talk invites us to look at how shared experiences, inherited narratives, and human connection shape who we are and where we are going.

Presented as part of TEDxArada’s theme, “The Seriousness of Play,” the talk encourages us to see play not simply as entertainment, but as a way of exploring identity, connection, and the possibilities of a shared future. Chapi Mwango is a Policy Professional and storyteller whose work explores the intersection of identity, leadership, and human connection across África. Born between Zambian and Ethiopian heritage and raised in Addis Ababa, his journey across cultures and continents has shaped a deeply reflective perspective on belonging, governance, and shared destiny. Through his work within development and public speaking, Chapi is passionate about building bridges between people, ideas, and generations. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Alan y papa. Creciendo en azul | Fernando Capurro | TEDxEsquel
recentItems.description:
Un repaso por la vida de mi hijo mayor, Alan , y como su autismo fue y es sinónimo de enseñanza y superación para él mismo  y para mí. El valorar las pequeñas cosas como importantes y lo que parece una tragedia solo un mal momento.
Sin lenguaje, te podes comunicar. Sin avances madurativos, puedes madurar. O sea crecer y hacerlo juntos  Entrenador de handball de más de 40 años, padre y esposo apasionado y amante perruno hasta la médula. Y que fue aprendiendo, de mas grande, a ser mejor padre. Una “Carrera” sin fin. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
